rule: Hand chronology, checked against Wikidata identities before any probe. Do not add or remove events after seeing the engine score.
validation: A direct event names a person, a place, and a date that standard biographies agree on.
An imprecise event is the same fact with a year or a season instead of a day.
A redundant event is the same fact under another name and must not be counted twice.
An off-topic event belongs to another life.
A wrong-place event moves a real fact to a place where it did not happen.
A partial date keeps the year or the season and does not invent a day.
A missing-coordinate event can be real while the gazetteer has no point.
A legendary or contested story is not an established fact.
An absent event is real and searchable, and this corpus or this short extract may not contain it.

persons.catalog_query: title_t:(Lonato OR Millesimo OR Mondovi OR Rivoli) AND (Napoleon OR Bonaparte)

Combat at Millesimo on 13–14 April 1796.
Combat at Mondovì on 21 April 1796.
Passage of the bridge at Lodi on 10 May 1796.
The bridge at Lodi is the same combat as Lodi.
Battle of Lonato on 3 and 4 August 1796.
Battle of Castiglione on 5 August 1796.
Battle of Arcole, 15–17 November 1796.
Battle of Rivoli on 14–15 January 1797.
Mantua surrendered on 2 February 1797.
Treaty of Campo Formio, 17 October 1797.
Armistice of Cherasco, 28 April 1796.
Napoleon held court at Mombello in June 1796. The fact does not require a map point.
The campaign opens in the spring of 1796. The day is not one event.

The imperial coronation is 1804, not the Italian campaign of 1796.
The discovery of radium is Marie Curie's, not this campaign.

persons.label: Victor Hugo
persons.catalog_query: title_t:(Hugo) AND (Guernesey OR Jersey OR Misérables OR Misérables)

events.claim: Born in Besançon on 26 February 1802.
Married Adèle Foucher on 12 October 1822.
Léopoldine drowned at Villequier on 4 September 1843.
Exile in Jersey from 1852.
Residence at Hauteville House, Guernsey, from October 1855.
Les Contemplations published in 1856.
Les Misérables published in 1862.
Returned to Paris on 5 September 1870.
The exile covers the Second Empire. One year does not date every residence.
Marine Terrace is the Jersey house. A missing point does not erase the residence.
The shortest correspondence with a publisher is told as apocryphal.
The exile was in the Channel Islands, not Moscow.
Austerlitz is not an event of Hugo's life.
Born in Warsaw in 1867. The day is 7 November.
Polonium announced in July 1898.
Radium announced in December 1898.
Nobel Prize in Physics, 1903, shared with Pierre Curie and Henri Becquerel.
Pierre Curie died in Paris on 19 April 1906.
Nobel Prize in Chemistry, 1911.
The Radium Institute laboratory in Paris.
Died at Sancellemoz on 4 July 1934.
The pitchblende work is a campaign of years, not one day.
Penicillin is not Curie's discovery.
The 1911 public scandal is contested personal history, not a scientific discovery.
Lonato is not Curie's life.

Entered Francis I's service and lived at Clos Lucé from 1516.
Died at Amboise on 2 May 1519.
The Vitruvian Man is placed around 1490.
A bicycle among his drawings is not an established invention.
Rivoli is not Leonardo's life.

Tutored Alexander, traditionally from 343 BC, through later biographies.
Opened the Lyceum around 335 BC.
Died at Chalcis in 322 BC.
The story that he drowned himself in the Euripus is not an established fact.
Polonium is not an Aristotelian event.

Rivoli is not her life.
